title: The map that lied
spec: M11 · one commit, no rebuild, and the gate that caught it
intro: The code moved. The graph did not. The agent answered anyway — instantly, authoritatively, and wrong. Watch the failure happen with every light green, then watch sixty lines of CI refuse to let it through.

provenance.source: a narrated session over labs/sample-project; every command, message and exit code is copied from labs/M11-freshness-gate/solution/freshness_gate.py, cited per step

foot: Run it for real: labs/M11-freshness-gate/ — Step 2 is the one most "production" setups have never actually executed.

steps.title: A commit that changed the graph's shape — and did not rebuild it
narrative: A developer adds a second caller for decode_jwt: the notifications worker now verifies its own webhook signatures instead of trusting the bus. Two lines. They commit and move on.

The post-commit hook does not fire. Pick your reason — the Windows shell has no nohup, the extension allowlist drifted, the resource gate skipped under load, or somebody typed --no-verify. It does not matter which, because all four produce the same symptom and none of them print anything. The commit succeeds. graph.json keeps the mtime it had this morning.
steps.youDo: Reproduce the state without waiting for a real bug: git commit --allow-empty -qm "commit without rebuilding the graph"

terminal.text: git commit -qm "notifications: verify webhook signatures locally"
(no [enrich] output — the hook never ran)
git log -1 --format=%ct  &&  stat -c %Y graphify-out/graph.json

HEAD      1756377720
graph.json 1756349104        ← 7h 57m older than the commit

after.title: AFTER — the commit, but not the rebuild

steps.title: The agent answers from the old map, at full confidence
narrative: Nobody knows the graph is behind, least of all the agent. Someone asks the standard pre-refactor question — who calls decode_jwt? — and the MCP server answers in one round trip, from the copy it holds.

Read the response closely: it is well-formed, deterministic, provenance-tagged, and missing the caller added eight hours ago. Nothing in its shape reveals its age. The agent concludes the blast radius is one module and proposes changing the signature.

This is why the module insists a stale graph is worse than no graph. With no graph the agent reads files — slow, expensive, current. With a stale one it gets a fast, confident, wrong answer and has no reason to distrust it.
steps.claudeSays: The server did not lie. It served exactly what was on disk, which had stopped describing the repository at 09:25 this morning.

terminal.text: who calls decode_jwt? safe to change its signature?
graph_callers(symbol="decode_jwt")
{"callers": ["shared.auth.verify_token"]}

One caller, inside the same module. Blast radius is contained —
changing the signature is safe with a single call-site update.
✕ the real answer is TWO callers · services.notifications.worker breaks on deploy

steps.title: Why nothing warned you: four doors, all green
narrative: The instinct is to go fix the hook. The module's point is that fixing this hook does not fix the class of problem, because a rebuild pipeline has four independently documented ways to stop working while reporting success, and new ones ship regularly.

The fourth is the nastiest and the least intuitive: a rebuild can succeed completely and the agent still gets the old answer, because the MCP server loaded graph.json at startup and has no hot-reload. Fresh graph on disk, stale graph in memory, simultaneously — and no artifact anywhere records that the two have diverged.
So the defence cannot be "fix these four bugs". It has to be refusing to trust a freshness you have not measured.

cells: Git-for-Windows has no nohup; the detached rebuild never starts
hook's extension list diverged from graphify/detect.py; valid commits skip the rebuild
CPU > 50% → skip, retry "on the next commit" — which may be days away
rebuild succeeds; the running server keeps its startup copy until bounced

after.title: THE COMMON SYMPTOM — which is the opening

view.text: However the rebuild died, the artifact ends up older than HEAD. Four causes, one observable. That is what makes a single timestamp comparison a complete detector rather than a partial one.

steps.title: The gate: one clock against another
narrative: freshness_gate.py compares graph.json's mtime against git log -1 --format=%ct. Fresh means the artifact was generated at or after the last commit. Note it compares against commit time, not wall-clock age — a repo untouched for a month with a month-old graph is perfectly fresh.

Run it on a healthy repo and it says so and exits 0. Then make it stale on purpose — an empty commit is enough — and the same command turns into a stop sign: the lag in commits, an actionable fix, and exit 1.
Read the fix line all the way to the end. It does not stop at "rerun the extractor"; it names the MCP restart, because door 4 is not fixed by regeneration alone.

terminal.text: python ../M11-freshness-gate/solution/freshness_gate.py . --max-age-commits 0
FRESH: graph.json generated at/after HEAD commit
git commit --allow-empty -qm "commit without rebuilding the graph"
python ../M11-freshness-gate/solution/freshness_gate.py . --max-age-commits 0
⏸  FRESHNESS GATE — artifact clock vs git clock

STALE: graph.json predates HEAD by 1 commit(s)
  fix: python labs/shared_tools/kg_extract.py <repo> --out graphify-out/graph.json  (then restart any MCP server holding the old graph)
$? = 1   → pipeline blocked

before.title: PASS — exit 0, agents may trust the graph

steps.title: --cross-check: when the clock is fresh and the content is not
narrative: A timestamp can be current while the contents are wrong — a partial rebuild, a refused overwrite, a report and a graph telling different stories. Clocks cannot see that; counts can.

--cross-check re-extracts into a throwaway file and compares node and edge counts against the stored graph. Agreement prints CROSS-CHECK OK; disagreement prints DESYNC with both pairs and exits 1. The finally block deletes the temporary file, and that matters more than it sounds: a leftover .freshcheck.json becomes tomorrow's confusing fourth artifact.
Below, the sabotage is a fraud_check() call added to webhooks.py and committed with the graph touched but not regenerated — clock says fine, counts say otherwise.
steps.youDo: Re-run the gate with --cross-check after any commit that adds a function.

terminal.text: python ../M11-freshness-gate/solution/freshness_gate.py . --max-age-commits 0 --cross-check
FRESH: graph.json generated at/after HEAD commit
re-extracting into graphify-out/graph.freshcheck.json …
DESYNC: stored graph has 36n/22e, fresh extraction has 37n/23e
graph.freshcheck.json removed (finally: never leave a 4th artifact)

stored counts vs a fresh extraction
an artifact that is wrong and consistently wrong

steps.title: Where it runs, and what it deliberately will not do
narrative: Placement is the whole point: the gate goes before any agent-consuming step. A freshness check that runs after an agent has already acted on a stale map is a postmortem, not a gate. And it must block — warning-only freshness checks are ignored by their second week.

Notice what these sixty lines do not do: they never repair anything. They refuse to proceed and name the fix. Keeping detection and repair separate means a broken repair path can never silence detection.

Stay honest in both directions. Above the ~500-file floor the gate is cheap insurance against a rebuild cost that is genuinely brutal — betweenness centrality is O(V×E), and one 450K-node / 690K-edge monorepo was killed on a 96-core Xeon after 114 minutes without finishing. Below the floor, the whole pipeline is ceremony and the gate is guarding nothing. Measure which side you are on before you adopt any of it.

The module's exit exam is a single sentence you should now be able to answer mechanically: how would you detect a stale graph within 24 hours? "CI runs the gate on every push and blocks on lag > 0" passes. "The hooks handle it" does not.
steps.youDo: Add the gate as the first step of your pipeline, ahead of every job that reads the graph.

terminal.text: ci.yml

- name: Graph freshness gate
  run: python ci/freshness_gate.py . --max-age-commits 0 --cross-check
- name: OKF bundle lint
  run: python ci/validate.py knowledge
- name: Agent-consuming jobs
  run: ...        # only reachable if both gates passed
